fields.System.Title: RET-2 — Receiving returns
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Take goods back into the building and record their condition — without any of them becoming
sellable yet.

Scope

In. Receiving against an RMA, blind returns with approval, quarantine landing, condition
recording.

Out. The inspection decision — that is [RET-3](RET-3-inspection.md).

Design notes

RET-203 is the story that protects the whole epic. Returned stock lands in quarantine.
Always. There is no fast path, no "obviously fine" shortcut, no configuration flag that turns
it off.

Someone will ask for one, because it saves a step. It is the single most common cause of
reshipped damaged goods, and the customer returns it again, and the cycle repeats until
somebody physically intercepts it.

Enforce the quarantine landing in the service layer, and make the transition to available
require an inspection record to exist. Then the shortcut is impossible rather than merely
discouraged.

Idempotency on the return line. A return processed twice creates stock from nothing and
credits the customer twice.

Blind returns are normal. Customers send things back without an RMA constantly. Support it
with approval and an exception record rather than pretending it will not happen.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Returned stock going straight to available | [doc 09 §8.1](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Return processed twice | [doc 09 §8.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Quarantine stock never dispositioned | [doc 05 WF 9](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
